license_required.quote: A person shall not engage in the practice of medicine and surgery, podiatry, osteopathic medicine and surgery, genetic counseling, psychology, chiropractic, physical therapy, physical therapist assisting, nursing, dentistry, dental hygiene, dental assisting, optometry, speech pathology, audiology, occupational therapy, occupational therapy assisting, orthotics, prosthetics, pedorthics, respiratory care, pharmacy, cosmetology arts and sciences, barbering, social work, dietetics, applied behavior analysis, marital and family therapy or mental health counseling, massage therapy, mortuary science, polysomnography, athletic training, acupuncture, nursing home administration, or sign language interpreting or transliterating, or shall not practice as a physician assistant or a hearing aid specialist, unless the person has obtained a license for that purpose from the board for the profession.

exams.notes: Board may prescribe one or more examinations or approve national standardized examinations in lieu of or in conjunction with board-prescribed exams; board establishes passing levels.
exams.quote: Evidence of having passed an examination prescribed by the board which shall include subjects which determine the applicant's qualifications to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery

required.quote: The board of medicine, board of dentistry, board of physician assistants, board of podiatry, and board of nursing shall establish rules requiring a person licensed pursuant to section 148.3 ... who has prescribed opioids to a patient during the previous licensure cycle to receive continuing education credits regarding the United States centers for disease control and prevention guideline for prescribing opioids for chronic pain

value: CDC guideline for prescribing opioids for chronic pain (for those who prescribed opioids in prior licensure cycle), including dosage limitations, length of prescriptions, risk factors for abuse, and nonopioid/nonpharmacologic therapy options
topical_requirements.quote: continuing education credits regarding the United States centers for disease control and prevention guideline for prescribing opioids for chronic pain, including recommendations on limitations on dosages and the length of prescriptions, risk factors for abuse, and nonopioid and nonpharmacologic therapy options

available.quote: The board of medicine may accept in lieu of the examination prescribed in section 148.3 a license to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery, issued by the duly constituted authority of another state, territory, or foreign country. Endorsement may be accepted in lieu of further written examination without regard to the existence or nonexistence of a reciprocal agreement, but shall not be in lieu of the standards and qualifications prescribed by section 148.3.

requirements.value: Board may accept out-of-state license in lieu of examination; endorsement may be accepted without regard to existence of reciprocal agreement, but applicant must still meet all standards and qualifications of section 148.3. Reciprocal agreements subject to board discretion per section 148.3(4).

is_mandatory.quote: A person shall not engage in the practice of medicine and surgery ... unless the person has obtained a license for that purpose from the board for the profession.

title_protection.quote: A physician or surgeon may use the prefix "Dr." or "Doctor", and shall add after the person's name the letters, "M.D."

scope_protection.quote: A person shall not engage in the practice of medicine and surgery, podiatry, osteopathic medicine and surgery ... unless the person has obtained a license for that purpose from the board for the profession.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly making misleading, deceptive, untrue, or fraudulent representations in the practice of a profession or engaging in unethical conduct or practice harmful or detrimental to the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowingly making misleading, deceptive, untrue, or fraudulent representations in the practice of a profession or engaging in unethical conduct or practice harmful or detrimental to the public. Proof of actual injury need not be established.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual intoxication or addiction to the use of drugs
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Habitual intoxication or addiction to the use of drugs.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Fraud in representations as to skill or ability
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Fraud in representations as to skill or ability.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of untruthful or improbable statements in advertisements
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Use of untruthful or improbable statements in advertisements.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful or repeated violations of the provisions of applicable chapters
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willful or repeated violations of the provisions of this chapter, chapter 272C, or a board's enabling statute.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Sexual abuse in the fourth degree
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Sexual abuse in the fourth degree in violation of section 709.4A.
Fraud in assisted reproduction in violation of section 714I.3.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly making misleading, deceptive, untrue, or fraudulent representation in the practice of the physician's profession
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowingly making misleading, deceptive, untrue, or fraudulent representation in the practice of the physician's profession.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating a statute or law of this state, another state, or the United States which relates to the practice of medicine
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating a statute or law of this state, another state, or the United States, without regard to its designation as either felony or misdemeanor, which statute or law relates to the practice of medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having license to practice revoked or suspended or other disciplinary action taken by a licensing authority of another state, territory, or country
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Having the license to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery revoked or suspended, or having other disciplinary action taken by a licensing authority of another state, territory, or country.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly aiding, assisting, procuring, or advising a person to unlawfully practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowingly aiding, assisting, procuring, or advising a person to unlawfully practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being adjudged mentally incompetent by a court of competent jurisdiction
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being adjudged mentally incompetent by a court of competent jurisdiction. Such adjudication shall automatically suspend a license for the duration of the license unless the board orders otherwise.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful or repeated departure from minimal standard of acceptable and prevailing practice, or committing an act contrary to honesty, justice, or good morals
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being guilty of a willful or repeated departure from, or the failure to conform to, the minimal standard of acceptable and prevailing practice of medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery in which proceeding actual injury to a patient need not be established; or the committing by a physician of an act contrary to honesty, justice, or good morals

disciplinary_grounds.description: Inability to practice with reasonable skill and safety by reason of illness, drunkenness, excessive use of drugs, narcotics, chemicals, or mental or physical condition
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Inability to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery with reasonable skill and safety by reason of illness, drunkenness, excessive use of drugs, narcotics, chemicals, or other type of material or as a result of a mental or physical condition.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful or repeated violation of lawful rule or regulation adopted by the board, or violating a lawful order of the board, or violating terms of a consent agreement or informal settlement
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willful or repeated violation of lawful rule or regulation adopted by the board or violating a lawful order of the board, previously entered by the board in a disciplinary or licensure hearing, or violating the terms and provisions of a consent agreement or informal settlement between a licensee and the board.

definition_quote.value: Persons who publicly profess to be physicians and surgeons or osteopathic physicians and surgeons, or who publicly profess to assume the duties incident to the practice of medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery; persons who prescribe, or prescribe and furnish, medicine for human ailments or treat the same by surgery; persons who act as representatives of any person in doing any of the things mentioned in this section.
definition_quote.quote: Persons who publicly profess to be physicians and surgeons or osteopathic physicians and surgeons, or who publicly profess to assume the duties incident to the practice of medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery.

methods_authorized.quote: Persons who prescribe, or prescribe and furnish, medicine for human ailments or treat the same by surgery.

drug_authority.value: Licensed physicians may prescribe, prescribe and furnish, and dispense prescription drugs and controlled substances incident to the practice of medicine.
drug_authority.quote: Persons who prescribe, or prescribe and furnish, medicine for human ailments or treat the same by surgery.

license_status_types.quote: The board may, in its discretion, issue a temporary license ... The board may issue a special license ... An application for an administrative medicine license shall be made to the board ... A physician, who is a graduate of a medical school or college of osteopathic medicine and surgery and is serving as a resident physician ... shall be required to obtain from the board a license to practice as a resident physician.

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates must present a valid standard certificate issued by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG) or similar accrediting agency, and must provide satisfactory evidence of successful completion of two years of postgraduate internship or resident training (vs. one year for domestic graduates).
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: An applicant who holds a valid certificate issued by the educational commission for foreign medical graduates shall submit satisfactory evidence of successful completion of two years of such training.

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: Satisfactory evidence that the applicant has successfully completed one year of postgraduate internship or resident training in a hospital approved for such training by the board.

pain_management_education_required.quote: The board of medicine ... shall establish rules requiring a person licensed pursuant to section 148.3 ... who has prescribed opioids to a patient during the previous licensure cycle to receive continuing education credits regarding the United States centers for disease control and prevention guideline for prescribing opioids for chronic pain

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: The board of medicine must adopt rules establishing penalties for prescribing practitioners that prescribe opioids in dosage amounts exceeding what would be prescribed by a reasonably prudent prescribing practitioner engaged in the same practice.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: Any board created under this chapter that licenses a prescribing practitioner shall adopt rules under chapter 17A establishing penalties for prescribing practitioners that prescribe opioids in dosage amounts exceeding what would be prescribed by a reasonably prudent prescribing practitioner engaged in the same practice.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: A licensee shall have a continuing duty and obligation, as a condition of licensure, to report to the licensing board by which the licensee is licensed every adverse judgment in a professional or occupational malpractice action to which the licensee is a party, and every settlement of a claim against the licensee alleging malpractice.

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: A full and confidential report concerning any final hospital disciplinary action approved by a hospital board of trustees that results in a limitation, suspension, or revocation of a physician's privilege to practice for reasons relating to the physician's professional competence or concerning any voluntary surrender or limitation of privileges for reasons relating to professional competence shall be made to the board of medicine by the hospital administrator or chief of medical staff within ten days of such action.

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: Establish a licensee review committee for the purpose of evaluating and monitoring licensees who are impaired as a result of substance use disorder, dependency, or addiction, or by any mental or physical disorder or disability, and who self-report the impairment to the committee, or who are referred by the board to the committee.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: The board may, upon probable cause, compel a physician to submit to a mental or physical examination by designated physicians or to submit to alcohol or drug screening within a time specified by the board.

administrative_medicine_license_availabl.quote: An application for an administrative medicine license shall be made to the board.

scope__license_status_types.quote: Failure of a licensee to renew a license within the grace period shall cause the license to become inactive or lapsed.

The board may, in its discretion, issue a temporary license authorizing the licensee to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery in a specific location or locations and for a specified period of time
the board may issue an order to revoke, suspend, or restrict a license to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery, or to issue a restricted license on application
Suspend imposition of judgment and penalty or impose the judgment and penalty, but suspend enforcement and place the physician on probation.
Suspend the licensee's license to practice the profession for a period to be determined by the board.
Revoke the licensee's license to practice the profession.
The board may accept the voluntary surrender of a license if accompanied by a written statement of intention.

The special license shall authorize the licensee to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery under the policies and standards applicable to the health care services of a medical or osteopathic medical school academic staff member

A physician, who is a graduate of a medical school or college of osteopathic medicine and surgery and is serving as a resident physician who is not otherwise licensed to practice medicine and surgery or osteopathic medicine and surgery in this state, shall be required to obtain from the board a license to practice as a resident physician.
